create.name: Cheri Huber
create.bio:
Cheri Huber has practised and taught Zen for more than forty-five years, calling herself first of all a student of the tradition. Her approach, which she calls Awareness Practice, aims at the end of suffering that the Buddha taught, but with a light touch: she encourages humour, curiosity and kindness towards oneself, and she writes about the harsh inner voice of self-criticism as something to be seen through rather than obeyed. In the 1980s she set up a Zen meditation centre to carry this work, and it now runs most of its programmes online.

She has written some two dozen short books, hand-lettered and illustrated, including There Is Nothing Wrong with You, When You're Falling, Dive and Be the Person You Want to Find. One of the methods she has developed is Recording and Listening, in which students record what they want to hear, play it back and answer themselves with compassion. Her centre offers email classes in which she responds to students' practice, phone and video meditation groups, practice buddies and longer retreats, and she hosts a weekly call-in radio programme, Open Air. She also founded Living Compassion, a project supporting children in Ndola, Zambia.

courses.title: Email Classes with Cheri Huber
courses.description: Several-week classes by email: students do a short practice assignment and write back about it, and the anonymised responses and Cheri's replies are shared with the group. New classes run a few times a year.

courses.title: Recording and Listening Training
courses.description: A five-week group course by conference call teaching her Recording and Listening method, used to clarify what you want and to train attention towards it.

free_resources.title: Audio Books
free_resources.description: Recordings of several of her books, including There Is Nothing Wrong With You and The Fear Book, offered free by her centre.

free_resources.title: Virtual Meditation Groups
free_resources.description: Regular group sittings by phone and Zoom, guided by a trained facilitator, for practising presence with others.

free_resources.title: Practice Everywhere
free_resources.description: Short reminders sent several times a day as cues to stop, notice the breath and come back to the present.

free_resources.title: Open Air with Cheri Huber
free_resources.description: Her weekly call-in radio show, where listeners bring questions about practice and daily life and she responds live.
